sections.title: Employment Contract
sections.text:
Orchid, newly a Sniper Operator, faces every kind of trouble with composure.

She earnestly explains that she has merely changed her outfit and nothing else about her is different. Do you believe her?

sections.title: Token
sections.text: A scrapbook plastered with fashion designs Orchid has clipped from all sorts of magazines. Pick a style you like, she says, and she'll design you an outfit in a similar vein — free of charge.

sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Captain of Reserve Op Team A6, the Rhodes Island HR Department office's Person of the Year, and founder of the shipboard fashion magazine Orchid. At her own request, she has been reclassified as a Sniper Operator. She has retained her battlefield support capabilities while making considerable progress on the offensive side. On top of that, she frequently volunteers constructive suggestions over the course of her assignments.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 8%
Operator Orchid's surface crystals have visibly increased compared to a few years ago.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.25u/L
Operator Orchid currently shows no signs of acute lesions, and all other physical indicators are at normal levels for this stage.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
The magazine Orchid is, by now, known to just about everyone on Rhodes Island. Helmed by Miss Orchid herself and named after her own Operator codename, this fashion magazine astonishes with the thoroughness of its content and the professionalism of its perspective. Today, this editor has had the honor of interviewing the magazine's founder, Miss Orchid.
Editor: Miss Orchid, what prompted you to start this magazine?
梓兰：加入罗德岛以后，我一直在做的一件事，就是帮助感染者通过时尚与潮流的方式掩盖身体上的结晶。为了这个来找我的干员和病人……真的很多，只能说，大家也都是人，都有追求时尚的权利，我觉得挺好的。不过，来的人实在有点太多了，我就在想，与其让他们一个一个来，不如我统一教大家一些方法。
Editor: And so you founded this magazine?
Orchid: No. Honestly, the HR Department work alone kept me busy enough to die. The idea did cross my mind, but I never actually intended to make it happen.
Editor: Huh? Then—
Orchid: There was a stretch where Catapult and Spot got sick of me nagging and decided to find me something to do. They went behind my back and filed for the magazine's production, even put together a proper sample issue and gave it to me for my birthday. I was genuinely touched at the time. Looking back, it was unbelievably stupid of me. But it was already made, and I figured an opportunity like that doesn't come twice, so I took it over and have kept at it ever since.
Editor: Then the names listed in the staff credits—
Graphic Design: Spot
Editing and Proofreading: Midnight
模特：斑点、月见夜、泡普卡、空爆……
Contributing Writer: Catapult
Could it be—
Orchid: Hah. They were so sure I'd take it over—did they really think they'd get away clean?
Editor: I—I see. That said, the ship is full of magazines, workshops, and hobby corners that Operators have started out of personal interest, and for most of them, output and activity depend on how busy the Operator's missions are and how long they stay aboard. Yet Orchid is a monthly, and it hasn't missed a single issue since it launched. So even if the beginning wasn't the prettiest, the process and the result have been good—wouldn't you say?
Orchid: Is that so, Spot?
Spot: Just kill me. Don't make me do any more layouts. I only want to read comics.
Orchid: And Midnight?
Midnight: Have mercy, Miss Orchid. I have stared at the word “garment” so long that I am on the verge of complete collapse.
Orchid: Catapult?
Catapult: I never wrote this much even back in school!
Orchid: What about Popukar?
Popukar: I love being a model for big sis Orchid!
Orchid: Spot has honed his drawing, Midnight has less time to bother people, Catapult has time to study, Popukar gets new clothes to wear, and I get to do something I've always been interested in. That's not bad at all, is it?
小编：……啊哈哈，让我们来聊聊有关取材方面的事情吧！

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
After completing her report on that strange journey of hers, Orchid quietly submitted a request: she wanted to know why Dr. Kal'tsit had brought Popukar back to Rhodes Island in the first place.
Having learned the full picture of the Bubbly Realm incident, the Doctor and Amiya agreed the request was warranted. Until then, all anyone knew was that Popukar's eye was unusual—and one unusual eye is hardly a rarity on Rhodes Island. But Orchid's experience seemed to prove that Popukar's eye, and her origins, were nowhere near that simple.
This was not because Orchid distrusted Rhodes Island or Dr. Kal'tsit—quite the opposite. There was simply no chance that Dr. Kal'tsit did not know Popukar's origins. Why, then, was she keeping them hidden? That question lodged itself in Orchid's mind and would not leave.
At the meeting convened for this purpose, Dr. Kal'tsit began by offering Orchid an apology. What Orchid and Catapult had gone through exceeded anything she had imagined, and as a result she could not give Orchid a clear account of the connection between Popukar and Baowujia. She needed time to sort out the specifics.
On the matter that truly worried Orchid, however, Dr. Kal'tsit gave a clear answer. From the very beginning, in assigning Popukar to Squad A6, she had no intention beyond hoping that Orchid would look after her—and there is no environment now in which Popukar could feel more at ease. For the sake of Popukar's peace of mind, Dr. Kal'tsit likewise hoped that A6 would bind itself together more closely.
“Popukar is simply a good child growing up healthy on Rhodes Island. That will never change, no matter when.”
Orchid accepted that answer.
In the end, she did not care what secret lay buried in Popukar. It might be important, but not that important to her. Just as she hoped for herself and for everyone around her, all she wanted was for Popukar to go on living happily.
By the time the meeting ended, she had made up her mind—she had already told the rest of A6 about what happened in the Bubbly Realm once, but she intended to tell it again. This time she would be sure to dwell on the far too flighty blacksmith, the far too solemn general, and that far too strong princess.

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
Orchid has a good relationship with her family.
In this respect, she is something of an outlier within A6. Popukar was taken in by Dr. Kal'tsit; Midnight, like Spot, has all but cut off contact with his family; and Catapult, an orphan, does not even know her parents' names.
The other members of A6 do not shy away from talking about Orchid's family. They all know that her parents care a great deal about their daughter's health and never distanced themselves from her because of the infection, and that Orchid writes to them regularly to report on how she is doing. The members of A6 all consider this a good thing.
Orchid admits she has been fortunate in this. Her parents never restricted her choices about work or her future; when she was infected with Oripathy, they supported her decision to go to Rhodes Island, and they always told her the same thing—she could come home whenever she wanted, and they were willing to give up a great deal for her sake.
Her parents were always worrying about her, always asking whether she had any plans to come home—which was only natural. In many people's eyes, no matter how renowned a pharmaceutical company Rhodes Island might be, anything tied to the Infected has an unsteady future. To Orchid's family, life aboard Rhodes Island was, in the end, not a very good choice—
“……我和你母亲商量好了，我们可以卖掉家里的房子，搬去一个偏远一点的地方一起生活，我和你母亲可以照顾你，你不用担心任何事……我们相信罗德岛是一家不错的公司，但是，有什么比家人团聚更幸福的事呢？”
So her father wrote in one of his letters, and at the time she found that she had no answer to give.
What was she supposed to say? Tell her parents that work here was going well enough, and that she had made a bunch of friends who were odd but decent people?
And then what? None of that seemed to conflict with going home. No job lasts a lifetime, and no friends stay together a lifetime—but family is different; family is bound together by blood. What's more, her family loved her so much, and she loved her parents.
She has no grand ambitions. She thinks Rhodes Island's ideals are magnificent, and she is willing to do what she can for the Infected—indeed, by the time she came to her senses she had already poured several years into the cause. She has heard how the elite Operators think, too, but she does not believe she could ever be like them.
This, as it was, seemed like enough. Once her condition worsened a little more and she could no longer work, or for some other reason, she would leave this place, return to her parents, and quietly wait for death to arrive.
For an Infected, that would already be a happy enough life.
She had imagined it. Yet she could never bring herself to pick up a pen and answer her parents. Something held her back, and she could not put her finger on what it was, so she always hedged and avoided the subject.
And this was not the first time.

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
Back when she was not yet infected and still worked as a magazine editor, her parents used to ask her whether that was the job she had dreamed of. She had given them no answer then, either.
She loves fashion, and she loves tailoring. But was that the pursuit she should devote her whole life to? She could not reach a verdict. She could not simply stop thinking about the choices in front of her, so she thought about them constantly. To others, that made her look like someone who always had her future planned out—but only she knew that she had merely been lucky enough to have the right to choose in a few matters.
A choice that decides a lifetime is simply too hard to make—after all, a life is so long. That was what she always thought, though she could hardly use it as grounds to forbid her parents from raising the subject. Eventually, her parents stopped bringing it up in their letters at all, because they knew it left her torn. In the end, she knew this was the ultimate question that she herself wanted an answer to—
What is it that I want to do with my life?
And before she had found an answer, she contracted Oripathy. She came to Rhodes Island for treatment, became an Operator, took over as captain of A6—and in the blink of an eye, several years had passed.
She was still no closer to an answer to that ultimate question. What's more, the pain Oripathy brought was a constant reminder that her life was no longer as long as she had once imagined.
I'm done for. That was what she thought, back from Sargon and facing yet another letter from home.
More despairing still, she found that whenever the thought “a life is so long” crossed her mind these days, she would tack on a line in Spot's tone of voice—“Well, at least now that you've got Oripathy, it isn't that long anymore.”
别说长进了，感觉已经被这帮人给同化了……在泡普卡惊讶的目光中，她有些颓然地趴到了桌子上。
Come to think of it, over these past few years she really did not seem to have grown at all.
She thought of Penny and Jerry, and of the wedding dress that still appears in her dreams to this day. She had gone back over that night a thousand times, and still could not think of anything she should have done better.
She thought of the last thing Catapult said during the Zinogre hunt. Yes—she was always telling the people around her that life ought to have an answer, when in truth she had no answer of her own.
She was always like this—saying one thing while feeling another, demanding of others what she could not necessarily do herself.
Sometimes she rather disliked that side of herself.
Even after the whole grueling trip through the Bubbly Realm, the only thing that counted as a gain—apart from this set of gear and a few memories—turned out to be that she had become a little more honest with herself.
But when she turned her attention back to how to reply to her parents' letter, she was somewhat surprised to find that this time, beyond the usual updates and pleasantries, there was something else she wanted to write.
“……我向你们介绍过很多次我的队友们，但是，大家一直没有什么机会见面聊聊。我最近在想，或许下次去哥伦比亚出外勤的时候，我可以带他们见见你们。”
She wrote that passage down almost as a matter of course.
This was, of course, not an answer.
It was only that, sometimes, being a little more honest with yourself means letting go of a few fixations. Perhaps there are jobs you can do for a lifetime. Perhaps there are friends you can keep for a lifetime. Perhaps none of it is in conflict.
She decided to give it a try.

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
Orchid has been showing up at the training grounds far more often than she used to.
It has not drawn attention the way Catapult's transformation did—Orchid has always been the diligent type when it comes to training, so to everyone else she simply seems a little more enthusiastic than before.
Dobermann, however, being her instructor, still noticed a few subtle changes.
In the past, Orchid completed her training only to meet the standards expected of an Operator; she had no drive to push her combat ability beyond that. But since returning from Sargon, changing out her whole set of gear, and even switching her tactical role, Orchid has genuinely changed in that respect.
But Dobermann also knew this could not simply be summed up as Orchid wanting to get stronger, or Orchid developing ideas about combat. You only had to stand beside her and watch how she trained to understand that.
It was more as though she were searching for something in combat.
Before one training session, Dobermann brought the subject up with Orchid.
“……站定、搭弦、瞄准、拉弓、射箭。射箭的步骤就和设计服装一样简单好懂。”面对杜宾这个打了多年交道的教官兼朋友，梓兰认真地想了想这个问题。
“So you think it has something in common with your hobby?”
“不。”梓兰摇了摇头，“设计服装需要去想很多事情，它需要创造力。而射箭……对我来说，重要的可能是射箭时我可以只用瞄准目标，不用去想任何其他事情。”
Orchid paused, and it seemed to take some effort before she got the next sentence out. “I can control it. No—I should say it's something I can control completely.”
“Control?” Dobermann was a little taken aback to hear that word come out of Orchid's mouth.
“对。我以前听说过，通过叠衣服、打扫卫生这些小事，人能够从中一点一点积累自己对生活的掌控感，最后获得面对生活的自信。我以前是不相信这些的，但是……”梓兰一边说着，一边拿起手中的弓，站定、搭弦、瞄准、拉弓、射箭，箭矢正中靶心，“在射箭的过程中，我确实感觉好像能够掌控自己一点了。”
“What surprises me is that you, of all people, need a method like that to control yourself.”
“Honestly, it surprises me too.” Orchid gave a slightly helpless smile. “But how should I put it—I was never someone who felt confident about everything to begin with, and I don't know whether this feeling is actually good for anything. It's just that these days, whenever something's weighing on me, I find myself wanting to come practice with the bow.”
With that, Orchid picked up her bow and arrows and headed for the training grounds. Watching her go, Dobermann was glad she had found a new interest—and puzzled that she remained so unaware of a certain thing.
“Does she realize that simply setting her stance, nocking, aiming, drawing, and loosing—and hitting the target every time—is not something everyone can do?”
